metadata.Description: JCoLA is a Japanese Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability consisting of 10,020 sentences annotated with binary acceptability judgments.
metadata.Paper Title: JCoLA: Japanese Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability
metadata.Abstract: This paper introduces JCoLA, a Japanese Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability, consisting of 10,020 sentences annotated with binary acceptability judgments. The sentences are manually extracted from linguistics textbooks, handbooks, and journal articles. JCoLA is split into in-domain data and out-of-domain data, the latter categorized by 12 linguistic phenomena. The paper evaluates the syntactic knowledge of 9 different types of Japanese language models on JCoLA, finding that while several models surpass human performance on in-domain data, none exceed human performance on out-of-domain data.
